title: Compact tool-spec IDL and repair-snippet validation for runtime
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Tool/function-call parameter validation is currently a patchwork of ad-hoc JSON Schema fragments, SDK-specific coercions, and unhelpful runtime errors. This leads to frequent developer confusion, flaky fallbacks, and high support load.

Goal: Define a compact, deterministic IDL (tool-spec grammar) that compiles to a small runtime descriptor used by the validator and SDKs. The IDL should support: strong primitive typing, explicit optional/required semantics, trimmed defaults, union/variant declarations, deprecation notes, and an extensible metadata slot for telemetry. Critically, the validator must provide actionable repair snippets and a machine-friendly error code that SDKs can map to localized messages and automated repair attempts (coercion modes).

Out of scope: full JSON Schema v7 compatibility and automatic schema inference from examples. We will provide an importer for legacy JSON Schema but not attempt 1:1 parity in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: IDL grammar RFC published and approved by PM/Design/Infra
Compiler that converts the IDL to a minimal runtime descriptor (compact JSON) and unit tests covering core constructs
Runtime validator integrated into the request path with two validation modes: strict and assistive
Error payload includes stable error_code, human_message, and repair_snippet (example JSON patch or field-level suggestion)
SDK mapping doc showing how the validator payload surfaces in JS/Python SDKs and how to enable automatic coercion with opt-in
End-to-end test exercising: missing required field -> assistive suggestion -> developer applies suggestion -> request accepted
technical_notes: IDL is intentionally smaller than JSON Schema: target feature set = primitives, enums, unions, optional/default, objects, arrays, and annotations. No arbitrary "if/then" logic.
Runtime descriptor layout: fields = [{name,type,required,default,deprecation,meta}]. Keep descriptor size < 2KB for common tool manifests to avoid token bloat in hosted flows.
Validation modes: strict (reject -> code VALIDATION.STRICT), assistive (reject + repair_snippet -> code VALIDATION.ASSISTIVE). SDKs can choose to auto-apply repair snippets when developer opts in.
Design for telemetry: include meta.validation_path and meta.hint_score to prioritize suggestions in the Console UX and Optimize recommendations.

Repair-snippet format: small JSON snippet or example value plus short natural-language rationale. Example: {"patch": {"parameters": {"max_results": 10}}, "explanation": "missing integer -> default applied"}
We will maintain a mapping table of validator error codes -> localized message keys in the i18n repo for Console/SDK UX.
Security: never include secrets in repair_snippet. Add sanitizer to strip values for logged snippets. Mark security_review_required = true for the schema compiler in this ticket.
implementation_plan: W1: Draft IDL RFC and minimal parser prototype (PEG grammar) - owner: Arjun
W2: Compiler that emits runtime descriptor and a small schema linter used in CI - owner: infra-eng
W3: Runtime validator library integrated into runtime path and a helper in SDKs to surface repair_snippet - owner: runtime team
W4: Instrumentation and telemetry keys + Console surface for repair suggestions and diagnostic hints - owner: observability
W5: Docs and SDK examples, plus migration guide for existing tool manifests - owner: devx
tests: Unit: parser handles unions and deprecated fields with expected AST
Unit: compiler produces runtime descriptor that round-trips to the parser
Integration: validator returns assistive repair_snippet for missing required scalar and for enum mismatch
E2E: JS SDK test that applies repair snippet automatically when opt-in is enabled
Fuzz: random manifests to ensure validator never throws and returns structured error payloads
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal teams opt-in to assistive mode via runtime flag for 2 weeks
Beta: open to early customers with feature flag + telemetry collection
GA: default to strict mode for user requests but surface assistive suggestions in Console and SDKs; document opt-in coercion behavior
Migration: provide conversion tool for existing JSON Schema manifests and a CLI linter to surface risky patterns
